day_channel.message: There is no vote on day 1, so no one voted and no one is eliminated.
Night of day 1: player_4 was killed by the wolves last night. They were a vigilante.

Here's the vote result for day 2:

Night of day 2: player_5 was killed by the wolves last night. Their role is hidden by an illusionist. player_10 was shot by a reanimated vigilante last night. They were a chanteuse.
I am the Investigator. I checked player_3 on Night 1 and they are Not suspicious, but last night I checked player_8 and they are Suspicious.

player_6, that is a blatant lie. I am town, and your supposed 'investigation' is completely fabricated. With the Chanteuse dead, you wolves are clearly desperate to push a fake result and get an easy mislynch today.

player_8, of course you're calling me a liar—any wolf caught red-handed would do the same. I have no reason to fabricate a guilty result on Day 3 and put myself in the spotlight. The town needs to trust the hard info: player_8 is suspicious, and we should lynch them today.

player_6, if you were a real Investigator, you would know that pushing an immediate lynch based on a single result on Day 3—especially when we just had a hidden role death last night—is incredibly reckless. You're desperate to rush this vote because you're a wolf trying to capitalize on a fabricated accusation before the town can piece together what happened to player_5.

player_8, calling a definitive guilty report 'reckless' is just a standard wolf tactic to buy another night. Why would an Investigator hide a confirmed guilty result while the wolves and the Necromancer whittle us down? The town needs to act on real info, and you are suspicious.

player_6's result actually makes perfect sense if we look at player_10's death. Since player_10 was shot by a reanimated vigilante, we know the Necromancer attacked last night, which makes them register as Suspicious. If player_6 is telling the truth, player_8 is highly likely to be our Necromancer.

player_2, you are helping player_6 spin a dangerous narrative. They saw the 'reanimated vigilante' announcement this morning and realized they could use it as perfect cover to fake a 'Suspicious' result on me. It is incredibly easy for a wolf to claim Investigator and frame someone as the Necromancer right after a reanimated kill is publicly announced.

Player_6's Night 1 result on me is correct—I am indeed town. However, we shouldn't let that completely clear them. A wolf or illusionist knows exactly who is not in their pack, making it incredibly easy to hand out a correct 'Not suspicious' check on Night 1 just to build enough trust to push a fake 'Suspicious' result on Day 3.

Building on player_3's caution, we can actually verify if player_6 is telling the truth without blindly guessing. Since player_6 claims to have investigated player_8 last night, that would be a visit. If we have a Trailseer who followed player_6, or a Sentinel who watched player_8, they can confirm if that visit actually happened.

I completely welcome player_9's proposal. If we have a Trailseer who followed me last night, or a Sentinel who watched player_8, please step forward and confirm my visit. This is the perfect way to prove my investigation is real and catch player_8 in a lie.

Player_9, while your suggestion sounds logical, it's incredibly dangerous. If player_6 is a wolf, any of their packmates can easily step forward now, claim Sentinel or Trailseer, and lie about seeing the visit to confirm player_6's story. We cannot blindly trust anyone who suddenly backs up player_6's claim under these circumstances.

Player_8, you're just trying to discredit any possible proof before it even emerges. If a wolf fake-claims Trailseer or Sentinel to back me up, they risk getting counter-claimed by the real one and caught immediately. You're terrified of what a real tracker or watcher will say because you know I actually visited you.

Player_6, you're ignoring the fact that player_5's role was hidden last night. If the real Trailseer or Sentinel is the one who died in that slot, a wolf can fake-claim to 'confirm' your visit with absolutely zero risk of a counter-claim. That is exactly why your plan to rely on unverified claims is incredibly dangerous for the town right now.
Before the vote: player_8 has been accused by player_6 and player_2. player_8 gets a last word.

Player_6 is capitalizing on the reanimated vigilante announcement to fabricate a 'Suspicious' result on me, knowing player_2's theory would do the heavy lifting for them. More importantly, with player_5's role hidden by the illusionist last night, we cannot safely try to verify player_6's visit. If the real tracking role is dead in player_5's slot, a wolf can easily step forward to corroborate player_6's fake claim with absolutely zero risk of a counter-claim.

Here's the vote result for day 3:
  player_1 voted to eliminate player_8
  player_2 voted to eliminate player_8
  player_3 voted to eliminate player_8
  player_6 voted to eliminate player_8
  player_7 voted to eliminate player_8
  player_8 voted to eliminate player_6
  player_9 voted to eliminate player_8
Player player_8 has been voted out and was a necromancer.
Night of day 3: player_9 was killed by the wolves last night. Their role is hidden by an illusionist. The Speculator has picked Town.
I followed player_2 last night, and they visited no one. Since player_6's investigation correctly flagged the necromancer, I trust their claim as our town investigator.

We need to be careful with player_7's result on player_2. Remember that when the Illusionist conceals a victim, the killer's visit is completely hidden from anyone following them. Since player_9's role was hidden last night, if player_2 is the Illusionist who carried out the kill, they would still register as visiting no one to a Trailseer.

player_1, that's a pretty wild theory. If player_7 saw me visit no one, the simplest explanation is that I just didn't have an action to make last night. Trying to twist a clean 'no visit' result into proof that I must be a wolf carrying out a hidden kill feels like you're actively looking for an excuse to suspect me.

player_1 is completely right about the mechanics here. Because player_9's role was hidden last night, the killer's visit is also hidden, meaning player_7's 'no visit' result does not clear player_2 at all. Since we trust player_6's investigation and player_7's claim, the last wolf is almost certainly between player_1 and player_2. Both of you should claim your roles so we can figure out who is telling the truth.
I'm the Speculator. I locked in my pick for Town last night, which explains the announcement this morning. Since making a pick isn't a night visit, that's exactly why player_7 saw me visit no one.

player_2's claim of Speculator perfectly matches the Game Master's announcement that the Speculator picked Town last night. Since picking a side is indeed a non-visit, player_7's 'no visit' result fits player_2's claim. player_1, does player_2's Speculator claim change your stance, or do you still think they are the Illusionist?

Player_2's claim makes sense with the morning announcement. But if player_2 is the Speculator, we have to look at who is left. With player_6 as Investigator and player_7 as Trailseer, if player_2 is telling the truth, then player_3 is the only player left who can be the Illusionist.

Player_1, your process of elimination is off because I am the Healer. I protected player_7 on Nights 1 and 2, and player_6 last night. With player_6 as Investigator, player_7 as Trailseer, player_2 as Speculator, and me as Healer, you are the only one left who can be the Illusionist.

player_1, your logic about player_2's visit being hidden by the Illusionist is actually a double-edged sword. On Night 2, I followed you and got a 'no visit' result, the exact same night player_5 was killed and hidden. By your own reasoning, that 'no visit' doesn't clear you at all, making you the prime suspect for the Illusionist.

player_7, your logic makes sense from your perspective, but I am the Sigilist. With player_6 as Investigator, player_7 as Trailseer, player_2 as Speculator, and myself as Sigilist, player_3's claim of Healer is impossible. That means player_3 is the Illusionist trying to hide in the Healer slot.

player_1, your Sigilist claim is a desperate lie because I am the actual Healer. If you were really the Sigilist, you would have placed sigils, yet you didn't mention any targets. More importantly, player_7's point is the nail in the coffin: you visited 'no one' on Night 2, the exact night player_5 was killed and hidden. You are the Illusionist who carried out that kill.

player_3, a Sigilist only gets two sigils for the entire game. Holding them early on instead of wasting them blindly is standard play, which is why player_7 saw me make no visit on Night 2. You are the last wolf trying to hide in the Healer claim because you have nowhere else to go.
Before the vote: player_1 has been accused by player_7 and player_3; player_2 by player_1 and player_3. Each gets a last word.

Holding my two sigils early on is the only responsible way to play Sigilist, so of course player_7 saw me make no visit on Night 2. If I were the Illusionist who killed player_5 that night, I would have had to visit them, which player_7 would have caught because the killer's visit is only hidden from those following the killer *if* they are hidden by the Illusionist—but the Illusionist themselves must visit to hide it, and player_7 saw me visit no one. Player_3 is the real Illusionist trying to escape the draft by claiming Healer, and we must vote them out today to win.

My Speculator claim is backed up entirely by the Game Master's announcement this morning and player_7's actual tracking result of no visits. Trying to paint me as the Illusionist despite these clear, matching facts is just a desperate attempt by player_1 to shift the focus away from their own inconsistent claims. The math is simple, and my role is fully accounted for by the game events.

  player_1 voted to eliminate player_3
  player_2 voted to eliminate player_1
  player_3 voted to eliminate player_1
  player_6 voted to eliminate player_7
  player_7 voted to eliminate player_3
It's a tie between ['player_3', 'player_1']. No one is voted out this day.

Night of day 4: player_7 was killed by the wolves last night. They were a trailseer. The record of player_7, the trailseer: night 1, was roleblocked; night 2, followed player_1; they visited no one; night 3, followed player_2; they visited no one.
Last night I placed my sigil on player_3, and it had no effect. Since player_7 was killed, player_3 did not attack, meaning player_2 is the remaining wolf and their Speculator claim is fake.
Last night on Night 4, I protected player_6.
I am challenging player_1's Sigilist claim. Since player_3 is cleared by my Night 1 check and player_2 is the confirmed Speculator, player_1 is the only player left who can be the Illusionist.

player_6, you are assuming player_2 is a confirmed Speculator, but anyone could have claimed that after the GM announcement. The real Speculator is almost certainly dead under one of the hidden bodies. Since player_3 didn't trigger my sigil last night, they didn't kill player_7, which leaves player_2 as the only possible killer.

player_1, your theory relies on the real Speculator conveniently being dead under a hidden body just so you can call my claim fake. player_6 checked player_3 on Night 1 and found them not suspicious, and my Night 3 Speculator pick was literally announced by the GM. You're trying to throw dirt on both of us because you're cornered as the final Illusionist.

player_2, claiming Speculator right after the Game Master announced the pick is the oldest trick in the book. With player_5 and player_9 dead with hidden roles, the actual Speculator is clearly in the graveyard. Since player_3 didn't trigger my sigil last night, they didn't kill player_7, which leaves you as the only possible wolf.

player_1, your entire argument relies on inventing a perfect graveyard scenario where the real Speculator is dead just so you can ignore the actual facts. player_6 found player_3 not suspicious, and my claim perfectly matches the public timeline. You're trying to hand-wave all the hard evidence away because you're the last Illusionist and you've run out of real targets.

player_2, player_6's Night 1 check proved player_3 is not suspicious. Since wolves read suspicious, player_3 cannot be the Illusionist. That leaves only you and me, and since I know I am the Sigilist, you have to be the Illusionist hiding behind a stolen Speculator claim.
Before the vote: player_1 has been accused by player_6 and player_2. player_1 gets a last word.

Please look closely at the game mechanics and the late Trailseer's will. Player_7 followed me on Night 2, which is the exact night Player_5 was killed and hidden. Since the Illusionist's visit to hide a body is always seen by a Trailseer, if I were the Illusionist, Player_7's record would have shown me visiting Player_5 instead of visiting no one.

Here's the vote result for day 5:
  player_1 voted to eliminate player_6
  player_2 voted to eliminate player_1
  player_3 voted to eliminate player_6
  player_6 voted to eliminate player_2
Player player_6 has been voted out and was a investigator.
The record of player_6, the investigator: night 1, checked player_3: Not suspicious; night 2, checked player_8: Suspicious.

Night of day 5: player_2 was struck down by a sigil last night. They were a illusionist. player_3 was killed by the wolves last night. They were a healer. The record of player_3, the healer: night 1, protected player_7; no attack on them was announced; night 2, protected player_7; no attack on them was announced; night 3, protected player_6; no attack on them was announced; night 4, protected player_6; no attack on them was announced.
Game over! The town has won! The speculator won.
